title: Three-color triangles
notes: On another visit, K-1 can move a single all-three cell (P5), optimize the subdivided board (P4), or change the boundary rule (P6). The older first-route packets hold P1, P2 (rows) and P4 (routes). Grades 2-3 can return to the local door cases (P3) before the impossibility argument (P5-6). Grades 4-5 can keep their minimum/maximum fillings and build the parity explanation from the local door cases (P3) to the proof (P5), with P6 as a separate test of the boundary hypothesis. A first visit ending with a well-checked filling leaves substantial mathematics for the next.

For four K-1 children, prepare four sets of fifteen counters in each of R, B and Y: 180 counters altogether. Two shared pair sets need 90. Keep the prescribed counter size and print scale; actual stock fit remains untested. The seven older children need seven sets of 6 R, 6 B and 6 Y for Problem 1 (126 counters), or four shared pair sets (72).

Guide F16-G-v4 follows the v4 student pages. In the older packets the rows problem is now Problem 2 and the routes problem Problem 4, Problem 1 uses counters, Problem 3 asks for different fillings rather than a complete catalog, and Grades 2-3 Problem 5 asks only about routes from bottom-side doors. K-1 Problem 2 is a hiding game for partners, Problem 5 records places with an X, and Problem 6 asks for two zero fillings without record boards. The keys and the mathematics are unchanged; the pages are unpiloted.
